title: VP-SDE marginals and Euler-Maruyama
goal:
Work with the variance-preserving SDE $\mathrm{d}x = -\tfrac12\beta(t)\,x\,\mathrm{d}t + \sqrt{\beta(t)}\,\mathrm{d}w$ (Section 3.4, Equation 11) with the paper's linear schedule $\beta(t) = \bar\beta_{\min} + t(\bar\beta_{\max} - \bar\beta_{\min})$ on $t \in [0, 1]$ (Appendix B, Equation 32).

`int_beta(t, bmin, bmax)` returns $\int_0^t \beta(s)\,\mathrm{d}s$.

`vp_kernel(t, bmin, bmax)` returns `(mean_scale, variance)` of the perturbation kernel $p_{0t}(x(t) \mid x(0)) = \mathcal{N}(x(0)\,m(t),\ \sigma^2(t))$ (Appendix B, Equation 33), so `mean_scale` is $m(t) = e^{-\frac12 \int_0^t \beta}$ and `variance` is $\sigma^2(t) = 1 - e^{-\int_0^t \beta}$.

`euler_maruyama_vp(x0, t_end, n_steps, rng, bmin, bmax)` simulates the forward SDE from $t = 0$ to `t_end` with `n_steps` steps of size $\Delta t = t_{\text{end}} / n_{\text{steps}}$. Each step is $x \leftarrow x - \tfrac12\beta(t)\,x\,\Delta t + \sqrt{\beta(t)\,\Delta t}\;z$ with $z \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$, where $t$ is the time at the start of the step. `x0` is an array of starting values; return an array of the same shape.
hints: With $\beta(s) = a + b s$, the integral is $a t + \tfrac12 b t^2$. The $\tfrac12$ on the quadratic term is easy to drop.
$m(t) = \exp(-\tfrac12 \int_0^t \beta)$ has the half inside the exponent. The variance is $1 - \exp(-\int_0^t \beta)$ with no half.
The drift term is multiplied by $\Delta t$, but the noise term is multiplied by $\sqrt{\Delta t}$. Use `rng.standard_normal(x.shape)` for $z$.
Use the time at the start of each step: `t = k * dt` for `k = 0, ..., n_steps - 1`.
